intro: When you search for a boundary surveyor near me, you likely need clarity on where your property boundary truly lies, whether you are buying, selling, or dealing with a neighbour. A boundary surveyor can investigate the legal boundary using title plans, deeds, and measured surveys, and can act as an expert if a dispute arises. We introduce you to a suitable UK surveyor who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a boundary surveyor usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for a boundary surveyor are facing a specific uncertainty about their property line and want expert evidence before taking any action.
needs: You are buying a home and want to confirm the exact boundary before committing, especially if the title plan is vague or features have changed.
You are selling and a buyer has raised a query about the boundary, so you need a professional opinion to move things forward.
A neighbour has extended a fence, built a structure, or planted hedges that you believe encroach on your land, and you want measured evidence.
You are planning work such as a new fence or extension and want to avoid future disputes by establishing the boundary line accurately.
You are already in a disagreement and need an expert surveyor to provide a measured survey or act as an expert witness.
context: HM Land Registry plans generally show general boundaries rather than exact legal lines, so they may not settle a disagreement on their own. A boundary surveyor will examine your title deeds, any older documents, and physical features, then carry out a measured survey to build a picture of where the boundary likely lies. This evidence can be crucial if you need to negotiate with a neighbour or take legal advice.

Disputes over boundaries can become costly and stressful, so getting early professional advice is wise. Many surveyors are members of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS), and RICS-regulated firms must follow professional standards, hold insurance, and offer a complaints process. You can check the RICS directory and ask about the surveyor’s experience with boundary matters before instructing them.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe the property, including whether it is residential or commercial, and its approximate location so we can match you with a local surveyor.
Explain why you need the survey—for example, a purchase, a sale, a neighbour dispute, or planned works—so the surveyor understands your goal.
Mention any relevant documents you already hold, such as title plans, deeds, or previous correspondence about the boundary.
Note whether the boundary in question is with a neighbour, a road, or other land, and whether there are any physical features like fences or hedges.
Say if there is an active dispute or if matters are urgent, as this may affect the type of surveyor you need.
Confirm your preferred timing and whether you need the surveyor to visit the site, so we can introduce you to someone who can quote accordingly.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the boundary surveyor
questions: What kind of survey will you carry out to establish the boundary, and what will the report include?
Are you a member of RICS, and is your firm regulated by RICS?
Have you handled boundary disputes similar to mine before, and can you explain how you approach them?
Will you examine my title deeds and any other documents I have, and is that included in your quote?
What are your fees and what do they cover, and will I receive a written quotation?
If the matter goes further, could you act as an expert witness or provide evidence for legal proceedings?

faqs.q: How can a boundary surveyor help if my neighbour and I disagree about the boundary?
faqs.a: A boundary surveyor can examine title plans, deeds, and physical features, then carry out a measured survey to provide an expert opinion on where the boundary likely lies. This evidence can help you negotiate or support your position if you seek legal advice.

faqs.q: Is a boundary surveyor the same as a building surveyor?
faqs.a: Not necessarily—boundary surveyors specialise in legal boundaries and disputes, while building surveyors focus on the condition of structures. Some surveyors do both, so ask about their experience with boundary matters when you enquire.

faqs.q: Will the surveyor’s report be accepted by a court?
faqs.a: A surveyor’s report can be used as evidence, but its weight depends on the surveyor’s expertise and the quality of the survey. If a dispute reaches court, you may need an expert witness, so ask whether the surveyor has experience in that role.

faqs.q: What should I have ready before the surveyor visits?
faqs.a: Have your title plan, deeds, and any correspondence about the boundary to hand, and note any physical features like fences or hedges that you believe mark the line. This helps the surveyor understand the history and focus their work.
